summary.plain_english: For every 1,000 users, about 7.7 more achieved conversion with the ad campaign than with the PSA. A difference this large is unlikely to be down to chance.
summary.reason: The primary metric improved significantly and by more than the practical threshold.
summary.headline: The ad campaign raises conversion by 43.1% vs the PSA (statistically significant)

key_numbers.label: Conversion: the PSA vs the ad campaign

caveats: PSA ids form a separate block (900,000 to 923,523); assignment unconfirmed.
Split confirmed as 96/4 only after a 95/5 check failed.
Exposure breakdowns are exploratory, non-causal; 4 of 7 buckets inconclusive.
No dates: novelty or wear-off cannot be checked.
No guardrail metrics defined; verdict rests on conversion alone.
Money impact needs a value per conversion.
next_steps: Marketing: keep the ad campaign running; it adds about 7.7 conversions per 1,000 users (now)
Data owner: confirm users were randomly assigned to ads vs PSA (within 1 week)
Finance: agree a value per conversion to price the 4,343 extra conversions (within 2 weeks)
Analytics: test ad frequency in a new randomised test before changing it (next quarter)
Marketing: keep a small PSA holdout when scaling to keep measuring the lift (ongoing)

summary.impact_headline: The ads produced about 4,343 extra conversions, roughly 30% of all conversions in the ad group
summary.so_what: Campaign value = 4,343 extra conversions × your value per conversion; compare it with the ad spend to judge return on investment.
